text:
marco: Heads-up — planning a small runtime patch tonight 21:00 PT (04:00 UTC). It’s a kernel micro-optim + quant profile swap (rtx-quant-v2). Goal: 10–15% token cost reduction on long-tail prompts without regressing latency. ETA ~30m for the change + 15m observation. Who can own smoke and rollback?

sasha: I can own smoke for eu-west-1. I’ll run perf checks, quick correctness samples, and KV cache warm. Do we have a canary slice reserved? :thumbsup:

ken: claim canary ap-south slot. I’ll coordinate with infra to cordon one slab and keep traffic limited to 5%. What’s the exact CLI/ops steps to flip the quant profile? post snippet pls.

lina: I’ll own rollback and incident comms if things look off. Quick question — is rollback a profile revert only or do we need to coordinate kernel driver rollback too? I’ll be available at start + 30m.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by marco: job-4821. Window start 2345678919. Auto-rollback policy: trigger on sustained error-rate increase >5% or p99 increase >100ms for 5m. Check runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-deploys

marco: Good. Plan outline: 1) cordon canary slab 2) apply kernel micropatch on canary 3) swap quant profile to rtx-quant-v2 on canary 4) run smoke checks (latency, errors, correctness samples) 5) if green, stagger to next slices (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with 10m observation windows. If any metric crosses threshold, rollback to rtx-quant-v1 and revert kernel.

marco: CLI snippets — use these in order:```bash
# cordon slab
redwoodctl slab cordon --slab canary-slab-7

# apply kernel micropatch (ops infra will stage)
redwoodctl runtime apply-kernel --slab canary-slab-7 --image engine-kernel:23.4.1-micro

# swap quant profile
redwoodctl runtime set-quant --slot canary --profile rtx-quant-v2 --apply

# rollback (if needed)
redwoodctl runtime set-quant --slot canary --profile rtx-quant-v1 --apply
redwoodctl runtime revert-kernel --slab canary-slab-7
```

sasha: Smoke checklist (I’ll run these sequentially):
- perf: p95/p99 vs baseline (expect p99 <= baseline + 50ms)
- errors: 5m error rate < 0.5% absolute and < +1% relative
- quality: run 20 golden prompts sample (fuzz + regression)
- KV cache: confirm warm hits > 70% after 5 min
- logs: no OOMs, no Loops in attention kernel

ken: Note: kernel micropatch needs a driver restart step. Plan to quiesce pods:```bash
# quick quiesce
kubectl scale deploy runtime-worker --replicas=0 -l slab=canary-slab-7
# restart drivers (infra only)
infractl node restart-drivers --slab canary-slab-7
# bring pods back
kubectl scale deploy runtime-worker --replicas=3 -l slab=canary-slab-7
```
Make sure persistent KV volumes are healthy; I’ll run fsck pre-start.

lina: Rollback procedure (I’ll execute): 1) set quant -> rtx-quant-v1 2) revert kernel image 3) if still bad, route canary -> fallback-model via routing policy and throttle traffic. I’ll announce rollback in #incidents and tag @support.

sasha: Dashboards I’ll watch: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/engine-canary (latency, errors, kv-hit, mem-usage). I’ll paste initial smoke outputs here once done.

ops-oncall: I’ll monitor SLO alerts and have escalation on stand-by. If anything spikes, ping @lina and I’ll mute alerting noise and escalate to SRE.

marco: One more: please capture a short sample of generated outputs (5 examples) before and after quant swap for quick human review. Keep an eye on hallucination or truncation issues.

ken: A small smoke log snippet I’ll post when canary is up:
```
[2026-03-17 04:10:21] canary-slab-7 worker-3: request id=abc123 tokens=512 latency=42ms p99 sample ok
[2026-03-17 04:11:03] canary-slab-7 worker-3: kv_hit=true cache_ms=4
```

sasha: ok I’ll run the golden-set tests and share pass/fail. If any of the 20 samples fail to match expected patterns we stop.

marco: Thanks — owners: smoke=sasha, canary=ken, rollback=lina, ops-monitor=ops-oncall. I’ll kick at 21:00 PT. Please ack here when you’re locked in.

ken: ack — will be on call 20:45–22:00 PT.

sasha: ack, I’ll post results in 21:05 PT.

lina: ack, standby.

marco: cool. tagging infra for final preflight: @infra — quick double-check on driver packages and live KV snapshots?

deploy-bot: Reminder: set quiet window in #support for 21:00–22:00 PT to reduce paging for expected transient spikes.

ops-oncall: noted, quiet window set. I’ll still watch alerts but suppress low-sev noise.

marco: Perfect — will post final "start now" message here before we flip. :rocket:
